Article Title: Can reputation of a celebrity be inherited, asks HC
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court , which has recently become the preferred place to secure "personality rights", has raised concerns over the expanding nature of such rights.While hearing a suit filed in 2023 over "misleading" YouTube content about the health and private life of Aradhya Bachchan, the minor daughter of actors Abhishek Bachchan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, the HC questioned whether a family's reputation flows down generations, how far personality rights extend and whether even "egregiously despicable" fake news can violate intellectual property rights."A certain last name has a reputation because of its eminence in a certain field of work. So, does that reputation, that you are couching as virtually as a trademark, flow down generationally? If so, up to what point?" Justice Anup J Bhambhani asked, flagging points that need to be examined in such cases.In 2023, a single-judge bench had restrained several YouTube channels from publishing misleading content on Aaradhya's health, calling such misinformation about a child "morbid perversity" and "completely intolerable in law", and saying every child is entitled to respect.- Abhinav Garg
Article Summary: The delhi high court has raised concerns over the expanding nature of "personality rights" the court questioned whether a family's reputation flows down generations. A single-judge bench had restrained several youtube channels from publishing misleading content on aaradhya's health.

Article Title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
Article Text:
SC gave the government two weeks to take a final call on introducing warning labels for packaged foods.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI ) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention."This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings."Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.The court, however, was unconvinced.The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions. The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness."In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings."We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI."The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.The issue has also been discussed by Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation, headed by Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora, who has advocated studying Singapore's Nutri-Grade model as a possible template for India.Separately, the Union health ministry has proposed displaying "sugar and oil boards" in schools, offices and other public institutions as part of a broader effort to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce excessive consumption of sugar and oil.
Article Summary: Sc gave the government two weeks to take a final call on introducing warning labels for packaged foods. Court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children. The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels.

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal on Friday said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief, Sukhbir Singh Badal , who was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.This marked the Badal family's first reaction to the attack on the former Punjab deputy chief minister."Truly grateful, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, for your personal call to inquire about Sardar Sukhbir Singh Badal ji’s health and for your good wishes for his speedy recovery following the dastardly attack on him inside a Gurudwara Sahib in Nanded, Maharashtra," Harsimrat Badal, SAD's only Lok Sabha MP, wrote on X.She also thanked the prime minister for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with the state police in the probe."Your concern, support and wishes during this difficult time mean a lot to all of us in the family, our party and to the people of Punjab. I am deeply touched by your kind gesture. I am also grateful to you for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with Maharashtra Police in the probe," the Bathinda MP added.On Thursday, Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Maharashtra’s Nanded district. The assailant was arrested at the spot.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered an inquiry into the attack and spoke to Sukhbir Singh Badal over the phone. The SAD president is learnt to have told Fadnavis that he was stable, ANI reported.Earlier, Badal was also targeted in an attempted shooting at the Golden Temple in Amritsar in December 2024 while he was performing “seva”. The attacker allegedly tried to fire at him but was overpowered before he could cause any harm.The 2024 attack took place while Badal was carrying out “seva” after the Akal Takht, the highest temporal authority in Sikhism, declared him a “tankhaiya,” or guilty of religious misconduct, over decisions taken by the SAD-led Punjab government between 2007 and 2017.The SAD and BJP, which currently lead the governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, are former allies. In 2020, the SAD ended its alliance with the BJP in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were later withdrawn.Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week, triggering speculation that the former allies could reunite ahead of the Punjab assembly elections early next year.
Article Summary: Sukhbir singh badal was attacked at a gurudwara in maharashtra's nanded on thursday. Harsimrat kaur badal said she was “deeply touched’ by prime minister narendra modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed “strong disapproval” of the Bar Council of India’s (BCI) now-revoked order barring the enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad’s NALSAR University of Law as advocates after a section of students objected to the university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.Kant, heading a bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said students have a right to protest peacefully and described the episode as a “dialogue” between him and the students."If students are protesting peacefully, who is BCI to take action? It is the right of the students to protest peacefully. It is a dialogue between students and me. No one else has to step in," the CJI said.Expressing its strong disapproval, the Supreme Court also stayed any coercive action against students or faculty by BCI or state Councils."It (the letter) was absolutely uncalled for," the bench added.The bench posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.On Thursday, the BCI had directed all state bar councils not to enrol any 2026 graduate of NALSAR University of Law as an advocate until further orders. It withdrew the directive within hours following an uproar on social media.In its initial statement, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council was examining allegations regarding a campaign against CJI Kant’s participation in the university’s convocation and had sought a report identifying those responsible.The BCI later modified its decision and allowed state bar councils to enrol the university’s 2026 graduates as advocates before withdrawing the notification altogether.The revised notification stated that the “vast majority” of students were innocent and should not be made to suffer for the alleged “misconduct” of a few.Around 450 graduating students of NALSAR had urged the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his alleged refusal to hear pleas concerning “police brutality” against students who had marched to Parliament on July 20 seeking the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG question paper leak in May. Pradhan’s resignation on July 25 brought the protests to an end.

Article Title: Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
Article Text:
Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment

NEW DELHI: “The elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.” Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.“Based on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),” Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems — pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says “at (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfaces” due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. “Since load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,” the communication says.“...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,” it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and France’s accident investigator under the ambit of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.
Article Summary: Airbus has asked air india to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. Airbus, in its initial assessment of the a320 flying from phuket to delhi on aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.

Article Title: 7 workers dead, 1 missing after water, debris enter under-construction tunnel in Uttarakhand
Article Text:

DEHRADUN: Seven workers have died and one remains missing after a landslide caused a cavity to form in an under-construction THDC tunnel at Mayapur in Pipalkoti, Chamoli district, allowing a rush of water and debris to enter the tunnel on Thursday evening, according to the latest official list. Fourteen workers were rescued and admitted to a hospital in Gopeshwar.The incident was reported around 7.05pm in the 2-km-long Tail Race Tunnel, where construction work was being carried out by Hindustan Construction Company (HCC).“There were 22 people inside the tunnel when a mix of slush and water entered it, trapping the workers inside. They were on the 2pm to 10pm shift. Fourteen workers were rescued, while seven have died and one remains unaccounted for,” an official privy to the development said.According to the official list of deceased, those who died have been identified as Pradeep Singh Panwar (31), a resident of Tehri; Mukesh, from Urgam in Chamoli; Dultam Sharma, from Bihar; Vijay (28), from Jharkhand; Jitendra Kumar, from Jharkhand; Lokeshwar; and Muneshwar. Details of the residences of Lokeshwar and Muneshwar were still being ascertained, according to the officials.The 14 rescued workers taken to Gopeshwar hospital were Sunil Jeevan (20), Havil Gudiya (27), Nistar Mijar (24), Vinod Ravana (46), Dina Barla (26), Khota Ram Bisra (22), Uday Singh (45), Tilak Raj (48), Chandan Kumar (39), Awadhesh, Nandlal, Rohit Pandey (20), Prem Singh (33), and Govind.The official list records Govind as discharged.The cavity had formed around 1.4km inside the tunnel, through which water and debris entered. “Pumps have been deployed to flush out the water,” a senior THDC officer said, adding that the cavity was likely caused by a landslide above the tunnel alignment.Soon after the incident was reported, personnel from the District Incident Response Force, local police and Central Industrial Security Force launched search and rescue operations. Given the seriousness of the incident, teams of the Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police, National Disaster Response Force and State Disaster Response Force were also deployed.Search operations were continuing late Thursday night to locate the worker still unaccounted for.
Article Summary: The incident was reported around 7.05pm in the 2km-long tail race tunnel. Fourteen workers were rescued and admitted to a hospital in gopeshwar. The cavity had formed around 1.4km inside the tunnel, through which water and debris entered.

Article Title: Park outside your Bengaluru home? It may soon cost up to Rs 25,000 a year
Article Text:
Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking (File photo enhanced with AI)

Rules propose

Private operators to enforce rules

Common parking portal planned

Penalties prescribed

Illegal parking on roads

Rs 500 for cars

Rs 300 for two-wheelers

Parking on footpaths

Rs 1,000 for cars

Rs 600 for two-wheelers

Key conditions

Residential street parking allowed only through permit

Permit valid for one year

Parking outside the permitted area will be treated as a violation





BENGALURU: The city is all set to put a price on one of its most contested public resources, road space.Under the proposed Greater Bengaluru Authority Parking Rules, 2026, residents who want to park their cars on the road outside their homes will have to obtain annual permits, with fees varying by vehicle type.The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and Metro stations.There are proposals for a complete ban on parking on arterial roads identified as high-density corridors by Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).It also seeks parking restrictions during peak hours on select arterial roads notified by traffic police.In addition, vehicles would not be allowed to park near junctions, bus stops, transit hubs, pedestrian crossings and footpaths, with detailed setback requirements prescribed under the rules.The proposed rules seek to significantly reduce on-street parking near public transport hubs.Initially, on-street parking would be prohibited within 150 metres of Metro and suburban railway station boundaries. The draft allows city corporations to gradually increase the no-parking zone up to 500 metres.The proposal is expected to impact several high-footfall Metro station areas across the city where commuters currently rely on adjoining roads for parking.In a shift from the current system, the draft proposes to authorise private operators managing public parking facilities to issue violation notices, collect parking-related charges, tow vehicles and clamp vehicles after being formally authorised by city corporations.The operators would be required to record video evidence of violations before towing vehicles, and all towing activities would be overseen by traffic police.To increase organised parking supply, the draft allows city corporations to lease vacant private plots and develop them into public parking facilities.Private landowners who voluntarily convert vacant plots into parking facilities would be eligible for incentives, including property tax exemptions.Owners providing mechanised or multi-level parking facilities could receive 100% exemption from property tax and service charges, while owners offering surface-level parking could receive a 50% exemption.The draft directs Metro, BMTC and suburban rail agencies to create off-street parking facilities on land available with them, particularly at interchange stations and peripheral locations, to encourage park-and-ride travel.Transit agencies may also offer discounted parking rates for commuters using public transport.All parking operators, city corporations and transit agencies would be required to share real-time information on parking availability, occupancy and pricing with GBA.The data would eventually be integrated into a common citywide parking portal and mobile application to help motorists locate available parking spaces and enable authorities to plan future parking infrastructure.Traffic police will continue to have powers to enforce no-parking regulations, tow vehicles and take action against repeat offenders.The draft also allows city corporations to increase parking rates based on demand and location and proposes higher charges for longer parking durations to discourage all-day occupation of valuable road space.
Article Summary: Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking. Residents who want to park their cars on the road outside their homes will have to obtain annual permits. The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and metro stations.

Article Title: 'Unfortunate, irresponsible': J&K CM Omar's Article 370, PoK remarks draw BJP fire
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday slammed Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah for criticising the abrogation of Article 370 during his Independence Day speech and accused him of creating an atmosphere of confusion in the Valley.Reacting to Omar's speech, leader of opposition in Jammu and Kashmir assembly Sunil Sharma said that the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019 strengthened the federal structure in Kashmir."The chief minister's speech was a bit regrettable. I would say this was an unfortunate and irresponsible speech because this is not a political stage. From this stage, there should be a speech for the unity, integrity and sovereignty of the country, a tribute to the soldiers, a tribute to the martyrs, and especially for the pride and honour of the Tricolour," Sharma said."I would like to tell the chief minister that it was after August 5, 2019, that this federal structure was strengthened. That is the reason why today every Kashmiri is humming Vande Mataram," the LoP said, adding that the chief minister's speech raises questions about what he wants to convey by "misusing this stage"."The whole of India accepts that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of them. People here are a strength, a power of this country.Not just here, but also those people across (the Line of Control) under illegal occupation. We consider them also an integral part of us, and deem them our companions," the LoP said.This comes after the chief minister, in his speech, referred to the protests in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir and said that the people on the other side of the LoC would have been protesting to rejoin India if Article 370 had not been abrogated.He said that the situation in PoK vindicates the decision of National Conference founder Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah and his colleagues to fight the Pakistan-backed tribal invaders in 1947.“When I see the situation today across the border and across the LoC, I realise that the decision taken by our leaders 80 years ago for us was the right decision,” the chief minister said. “Those who raised the slogan ‘Hamalawar Khabardar’ were right and the sacrifices they made were right,” Omar said.“Today I remember people like Master Abdul Aziz, a leader of the National Conference, who was brutally killed in Muzaffarabad (PoK) to stop those very attackers, to stop the tribals, to stop those infiltrators,” Omar said. “Today, when we see the condition of that part of Jammu and Kashmir across the LoC, we feel sad, we feel worried. For my part, I feel that perhaps if our situation had not changed in 2019, the people of that part of Jammu and Kashmir would be protesting to rejoin us today,” Omar said.“That part of Jammu and Kashmir is ours. We consider those people as our own. No one is a stranger. No one is an outsider. Even today, as per the law of Jammu and Kashmir, seats are reserved for them in the Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir, with the hope that one day those people will be able to use these vacant seats,” Omar added.
Article Summary: Jammu and kashmir chief minister omar abdullah criticises the abrogation of article 370 during his independence day speech. Congress, however, said there was no attempt to stop the full rendition and that Sonia was merely asking for a chair for party president Mallikarjun Kharge, who had been standing for some time.BJP spokesperson Gopal Krishna Agarwal, sharing the footage on X, accused the Congress of showing disrespect towards the national song. "The scene that has come to light today on Independence Day is utterly shameful."He said, "Sonia Gandhi's objection during the rendition of India's national song, 'Vande Mataram', and her questioning of Congress workers as to why it was being played exposes the Congress party's mindset."Agarwal said Vande Mataram represented more than a patriotic song, calling it a symbol of India's freedom struggle and national consciousness."Is this the same Congress that lays claim to the legacy of the nation's freedom struggle?" he asked.He also alleged that the Congress's alleged approach towards the national song reflected the party's "Emergency mindset"."The people of the country have rejected this mindset and will continue to reject it," he said.The Congress dismissed the BJP's claim and maintained that the full version of Vande Mataram was sung at its Independence Day programme.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh cited the party's historical association with the song and referred to a 1937 meeting of the Congress Working Committee in Calcutta, attended by several prominent leaders of the freedom movement."On October 28, 1937, in Calcutta, a meeting of the Congress Working Committee was held in the presence of Mahatma Gandhi, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Jawaharlal Nehru, Govind Ballabh Pant and C Rajagopalachari, and on the advice of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore, they decided that the initial stanzas of Vande Mataram would be sung at the Congress sessions," Ramesh said.Ramesh said Tagore had advised Nehru and Bose that the opening portions of the song should be used at Congress gatherings."Tagore gave the advice to Nehru and Bose that the first few paragraphs of Vande Mataram should be used, he said."We have been singing those lines in every session since them, our Seva Dal sings it, our workers sing it, there is no controversy over that," Ramesh said."He stressed that the complete version was sung at Saturday's event and said the issue had already been debated extensively in Parliament."This was discussed in Parliament for 16 hours. We put forward our views. I narrated the whole history around it which the prime minister and the home minister did not know. I informed MPs of the context in which the Vande Mataram decision was taken," Ramesh said."But today, at Indira Bhawan, the full version was sung, there is no question of a controversy over it," he added.Asked specifically about the BJP's allegation that Sonia had tried to stop the full rendition, Ramesh offered a different explanation for what was seen in the video."As the Congress president was standing for a long time, Soniaji was asking for a chair for him," he said.BJP spokesperson R P Singh also targeted Sonia over the controversy, questioning her alleged opposition to the national song."Why does Antonio Maino Ji hate Vande Mataram so much? When Vande Mataram was being sung, Antonio Maino Ji reportedly became so angry that she allegedly got agitated and asked her party workers to stop it. Why such hatred for Vande Mataram?"The row over Vande Mataram comes shortly after Parliament passed legislation dealing with disrespect towards the national song. The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed by the Lok Sabha through a voice vote on July 30, a day after the Rajya Sabha cleared it.The legislation grants Vande Mataram a status on par with the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
Article Summary: Sonia gandhi’s vande mataram row: bjp alleges ‘hatred’, congress calls claim false. Bjp accuses grand old party's former chief sonia gandhi of objecting to the national song. Congress rejects bjp's allegation. When vande mataram was being sung, antonio maino ji reportedly became so angry that she allegedly got agitated and asked her party workers to stop it.

Perhaps the real measure of progress is that there has been a shift, but still there is a long way to go.

‘What do you do?’Sounds like a simple question. But in India, the answer to this question determines your social status.Is there any scope?How much will you earn?What will people say?Some careers in India instantly earn respect. Others invite questions.So when a young person chooses a career, are they really choosing what they want or are they going for what society considers worth choosing?A 2018 Global Education Census by Cambridge International, based on responses from nearly 20,000 teachers and students across the world, including 4,400 teachers and 3,800 students in India, found that medicine and engineering continued to dominate career ambitions.The survey found that 23% of Indian students wanted to become doctors or dentists, while an equal 23% aspired to become engineers. Another 16% wanted to become software engineers, the highest proportion for this career among all countries surveyed. The findings also showed India's strong interest in scientific careers, with 8% of students saying they wanted to become scientists.Now, let’s figure out why that is so.While some students choose these careers out of genuine interest, others pursue them under pressure from parents and society.Another 2020 study published in the Int J of Indian Culture and Business Management found that parents, peers and societal expectations significantly influence career choices among Indian youth.TOI also conducted a survey to understand how society perceives different professions and whether certain careers continue to command greater respect than others.Among respondents from sectors including journalism, medicine and PR, we received 100% response in ‘yes’, agreeing that society accords greater respect to certain professions, with over 80 % respondents selecting both doctors, and IAS/IPS officers emerging as the most prestigious career choices, in second position was engineering.Around 74 % of them agreed that often-overlooked professions like nurse, police constable, mechanic, cab driver do not receive the same respect as traditionally prestigious careers in medicine and engineering.Somdeb Dhar Choudhury, one of the respondents and a PR consultant, said, “I grew up in an environment where engineering was considered the more conventional professional route. Many people in my extended family came from engineering backgrounds, and after Class 12, there was an expectation that I would follow a similar path.”When asked why he thinks PR receives less social recognition, he said, “In India, professions such as medicine, engineering and civil services have had a clearly understood social identity for generations. Families know what those careers involve, there is a visible educational path leading to them, and society has established benchmarks of success around them. PR operates very differently. Much of the work happens behind the scenes. ”When asked if the respondents ever felt pressured to choose a career mainly because of its title or status, half of them responded with yes. More than half chose yes when asked if their relatives ever suggested they choose a particular career.Rashmi N, former Army public school counselor, while speaking to TOI, says, “Peer comparisons lead to self doubt and career indecisions. Falling behind in academics and comparing grades with peers may also trigger withdrawal from friends, low self esteem and or lack of interest to improve.”On the other hand psychologists say the pressure to choose a socially accepted career may not always be obvious.Explaining the same, a Delhi-based psychologist Radhika Goyal said, “when motivation is driven mainly by fear, fear of failure, criticism, comparison or disappointing the family, rather than genuine enthusiasm. A student may perform well but still experience burnout, frustration or disengagement.”While parents may want the best for their children, it’s important to discuss what drives them to push certain careers over others.1. Job securityFor many Indian parents, a “good” career is still closely associated with stability, authority, financial security and social respect.Rashmi said that this may be because of job stability and authority.“Authority, financial stability & fame are the major factors influencing the perception of any career paths.”“For more affluent families, social status, community approval and family reputation can weigh heavily on career choices, while for families with fewer financial resources, immediate income and financial security may take precedence,” she said.2. Unfinished ambitions leading to societal comparisonsGoyal pointed to an often-overlooked factor: parents projecting their own unfinished ambitions or past experiences onto their children.“Parents may sometimes project their own unfinished ambitions, disappointments or experiences onto their children’s career choices, often with good intentions. A parent who could not pursue a particular career may believe they are protecting their child from the difficulties they experienced.”However, this dynamic appears to be changing among a newer generation of parents.Savita S, a parent of a 24-year-old daughter working in an HR firm, said, “I believe my children are satisfied with my support.”When asked about the typical ‘Sharma ji ka beta’ comparison, she said that parents are becoming more mindful of how their children respond to such pressure.“This kind of comparison is reducing day by day.”Now, if you’ve had your parents’ support, overcome societal pressure and chosen a career based on your own dreams, are you truly happy with that choice?1. PaycheckFor some young professionals, the pressure around career choices continues even after entering the workforce, with questions of money, job security and growth becoming important factors in deciding whether to stay or change paths.Aayushi, a journalist, while sharing her experience said, “I was satisfied with choosing a career outside the conventional mainstream, but was disappointed by the financial returns. I am satisfied in terms of doing something different from the generic league. But in terms of money, way too underwhelmed.”She also sometimes considered changing her career.2. Women face another layer of pressureA 2025 study published in thefound that women were more likely to change careers because of social expectations, especially after marriage, while men more often cited personal interests and changes in the job market.The gendered perception of careers can also influence how professions are valued.3. When your profession needs an explanationFor some professionals, however, the pressure is less about being forced to leave a career and more about constantly having to explain its worth.Somdeb recalled that this became apparent after he entered the industry. “If someone says they are a doctor, engineer or lawyer, people immediately understand the profession. In PR, you often have to explain what the job involves before people can understand its value. That lack of familiarity created more pressure for me than any direct opposition to my career choice.”
Article Summary: Poll vote & share your view what do you value more in a career? Social status job satisfaction financial security. What are the top careers in india? What role do parents & society play? 75 % of respondents selected yes when asked if their relatives ever suggested them a 'better' career.

Article Title: Armed Naxals gone, now identify & isolate 'dimagi Naxals': PM Modi on Independence Day
Article Text:

New Delhi: The youth took centre stage in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day address on Saturday as he unveiled a host of initiatives, including free online coaching and AI skilling, but also warned against "dimagi Naxals. ..looking for ways of violence and anarchy", who, he said, must be "identified" and "isolated".The PM's 13th consecutive speech from the ramparts of Red Fort, over 75 minutes long, was marked by repeated invocations of the youth, who were the face of the most consequential protest his govt has faced since 2014, leading to education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and a slew of legislative and executive measures to reform the examination system.The PM emphasised the threat "dimagi Naxals" pose even as his govt has largely eliminated "hathiyari Naxals" (armed Naxals). Modi has often used the term "urban Naxals" to describe sympathisers of the Maoist movement. His coinage of "dimagi Naxals" appears to be a nod to the belief in BJP circles that hardcore Left groups, especially AISA, the student wing of CPI(ML), played a key role in mobilising and sustaining support for the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest."These dimagi Naxals are looking for ways of violence and anarchy. They are resorting to various tactics to drag society to the wrong path. We must identify these dimagi Naxals, isolate them, and steer the nation's youth toward the mainstream effort of transforming India into a developed nation," he said.The challenge of 'dimagi Naxals should not be underestimated' as they used to have presence in "corridors of power", even as advisers in govt committees, he emphasised. BJP has accused Congress of keeping people with professed Naxal sympathies in committees that shaped policies during UPA's tenure in 2004-2014.PM Narendra Modi has himself revved up engagement with Gen Z of late, and used the showpiece annual event, in which he often lays out his governance agenda and sums up the country’s development arc since he took office in 2014, to unpack several programmes for them. This comes amid the assessment in political circles that there is a growing clamour for more and better job opportunities.Self-reliance was another key theme, with Modi announcing “sapta-dhara”, which will focus on seven different aspects of the country’s economy to ramp up growth.Fresh off a Parliament session, which was a virtual washout owing to the opposition’s protest against his govt on a variety of issues, Modi denounced his rivals as a bunch of doomsayers who draw perverse pleasure in keeping the country scared and worried, noting that they predicted the worst of fuel crises after the West Asia conflict broke out but his govt handled it ably. “Rumours were spread that petrol would not be available at petrol pumps, that there would be no gas, no diesel and no fertiliser,” he said.Acknowledging the financial burden of coaching classes on the poor and middle-class families, he announced, “We have decided to provide free online coaching for various examinations for the youth. We have digital public infrastructure; we have excellent talent and teachers.By bringing these resources together, we are going to build a complete network to provide free coaching to the youth of the country.”It will save these families thousands of crores of rupees and allow them to keep their children with them, he added.The PM had something for Gen Alpha as well: a nationwide talent hunt among children in 5-15 age bracket to give the selected players specialised training to prepare them as India looks to boost its standing in global sporting events. Govt will also develop a comprehensive civil defence programme, capable of addressing modern challenges and protecting citizens from contemporary crises, he said.

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary panel has taken note of a curious case involving emergency alert buttons in buses. Article Title: At BCI helm for 14 years, Manan Kumar Mishra faces heat over professional conduct
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BCI's controversial decision to bar 2026 law graduates from Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law from being registered as advocate, which it withdrew within hours, brought into focus the regulator's working which has been headed by senior advocate and BJP MP Manan Kumar Mishra for 14 years.A statutory body established under Advocates Act, 1961, BCI is mandated to regulate legal profession and legal education. It lays down standards of professional conduct for advocates, exercises disciplinary jurisdiction, and recognises universities whose law degrees qualify a person for enrolment. Section 7(1)(g) of the Act also gives it general supervision and control over state bar councils.But no provision of the Act gives it the power to enrol a person as an advocate which is to be done by a state bar council to admit persons as advocates on its roll. Clearly, the regulator ventured into the area beyond its domain by taking punitive measures against students, and upset SC which observed that BCI had no business to intervene in the matter.The controversy has put the spotlight on BCI's functioning on whether it has over the years been able to discharge its statutory duty to maintain the standard of legal profession and legal education. Going by a statement of Mishra himself, BCI has failed in its duty by a massive margin.An outspoken man who contested polls as nominees of BSP and Congress before drifting into BJP , has said on more than one occasion that 35-40% of advocates have fake degrees, and are practicing in the courts on the basis of fabricated degree certificates. The statement, while believed to be true by many, is an indictment of regulator and clear evidence that guard rails against serious malpractice have not been working.Another failure of BCI is in the field of legal education as it failed to maintain standard in view of proliferation of law colleges; some of them are virtually selling law degrees with students exempted from attending classes. It has regularly faced SC's ire for not infusing professionalism into the profession and not taking action against erring lawyers who keep resorting to strikes.
Article Summary: Bci's decision to bar 2026 law graduates from hyderabad's nalsar university of law from being registered as advocate has brought into focus the regulator's working. The controversy has put the spotlight on bci's functioning on whether it has over the years been able to discharge its statutory duty.

Article Title: PM Modi puts women's quota back on table, makes fresh pitch to opposition

New Delhi: PM Narendra Modi chose his Independence Day address Saturday to give a strong indication of of his govt's intent to revive the Constitution amendment bill to implement one-third reservation for women in Lok Sabha and assemblies, with a 50% jump in their overall strength from 2029, urging all political parties to ensure that it was rolled out as soon as possible.While it was widely speculated in political circles that govt was keen to revive the bill, which was defeated by the opposition in April, Modi put on record that the matter was on the agenda, boosting the prospect of Parliament being summoned as early as next month."Today, standing here beneath the shadow of the Tricolour on the ramparts of Red Fort, I pray to and urge all political parties to acknowledge the power of women. Let's step forward to uphold their dignity and ensure our mothers and sisters get 33% representation in assemblies and Lok Sabha as soon as possible," he said.What has enhanced the likelihood of the bill being passed is the defection of 20 Lok Sabha MPs from Trinamool Congress and six from Sena UBT to NDA and DMK's assiduous efforts, visible in the recently concluded session, to keep away from the opposition's ranks after Congress ditched it in Tamil Nadu to ally with Vijay-led TVK.NCP SP is being seen as another potential support.Congress accused Modi of making a "dishonest pitch" for women's reservation in his address, saying 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' was unanimously passed in Sept 2023, but BJP govt's "double standards" and "hypocrisy" had made sure it didn't come into effect from 2024.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh, in a post on X, said the party had stood firm on its stand to implement women's reservation from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections by retaining the current strength of 543 seats in LS.Modi said women served as public representatives in large numbers in panchayats to municipalities and municipal corporations, referring to their salience in local bodies on the back of reservation.Despite several efforts to reserve seats in Lok Sabha and assemblies, the idea had fallen victim to political battles for over 40 years, he said.He called it the need of the hour and told parties to join the cause. "You also take the credit, you also take the fame, but give rights to my mothers and sisters," he said, reiterating the pitch he had made before the failed bid last time.The monsoon session has not been prorogued, keeping open the possibility of govt summoning Parliament.
